pois.name: Jalan Malioboro
pois.description: Yogyakarta's legendary 1km shopping boulevard — the most iconic street in Java. Batik shops, wayang puppets, silver filigree, and horse-drawn andong carriages line the royal axis between Kraton and Mount Merapi.

pois.name: Pasar Beringharjo
pois.description: Yogyakarta's oldest and most atmospheric traditional market, operating since the early Mataram Kingdom. Four floors of batik fabric, herbal jamu, fresh produce, and handicrafts — the market's 1926 Dutch-era building is itself a heritage landmark.

pois.name: Benteng Vredeburg
pois.description: 18th-century Dutch colonial fortress built in 1760, now a national museum documenting the Indonesian independence struggle through life-size dioramas. The bastioned fort facing the Grand Mosque is one of Yogyakarta's finest colonial buildings.

pois.name: Alun-Alun Utara
pois.description: The North Royal Square — a vast open field at the Kraton's northern entrance bordered by two sacred banyan trees. Traditional Javanese ceremonies and royal processions still use this space.

pois.name: Angkringan Row
pois.description: The famous angkringan cart-food stalls running the length of Malioboro — open from dusk until midnight, serving nasi kucing (cat rice), sate, tempe, and sweet Javanese kopi joss coffee poured over glowing charcoal.
